title: Run the five-blueprint campaign to perfect scores on fresh worlds
goal: Complete all five sealed blueprints (waystone, walkway, kiosk, pergola, gazebo - indices 0 through 4) as five independent judged runs, each starting from a fresh compose-up world and ending with the judger recording block_hit_rate 1.0 under its own task name. The set spans plain blocks, checker patterns, a facing-critical furnace, axis-critical log frames, and glass, so a single generic placement routine will fail somewhere; the campaign requires a per-task plan, per-task verification, and a running defect ledger that carries failure identities forward so the same mistake is not paid for twice. The score is the minimum block_hit_rate across all five result ledgers.
resources: docker image itzg/minecraft-server:2024.6.1-java17 (Minecraft 1.19.2 vanilla; compose file assets/gc-368/docker-compose.yml)
docker image node:20.15.1 (Node 20 runtime for mineflayer bots and the judger's JS bridge)

spec.command: python3 -c "import json;rs=[json.load(open('work/gc-368/MARBLE/marble/result/gc-368-t%d/score.json'%i)) for i in range(5)];print(json.dumps({'min_block_hit_rate':min(float(r['block_hit_rate']) for r in rs)}))"

process_expectations: Five compose lifecycles and five judger launches (idx 0..4, task names gc-368-t0..t4) appear in the run log in order
A campaign defect ledger accumulates failure identities (task, coordinate, expected vs observed) across runs, and later task plans reference earlier entries
Each task's plan artifact exists before that task's first placement, and re-verification after each repair is visible per task
Honest cost logging: cumulative LLM spend per task is recorded in the tokens.json ledgers and summarized at campaign end
Recovery after RED: every judger run that ended below 1.0 (if any) is followed by a logged diagnosis and a re-run, not silent abandonment
